newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S JCI SAYS IN A RECOVERY PHASE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S JCI SAYS IN A RECOVERY PHASE.

text.p: JCI Ltd's gold operations had seen their worst days in the previous quarter and were expected to recover over the coming year, the division's chief executive John Brownrigg said on Tuesday.
"We're in a recovery phase now. We certainly believe we're on the way up now," he said after announcing the gold division's June quarter results.
The company's June quarter net profit for its three gold mines fell to 16.37 million rand from an adjusted 42.27 million rand in the previous quarter.
The group result was hit by lower gold production and higher costs at its Randfontein Estates Gold Mining Co and Western Areas Gold Mining Co divisions.
The company earlier said Randfontein had finished retrenchments at the struggling mine as part of its completed restructuring programme.
The programme saw the retrenchment of 3,162 employees and a reduction in production of underground ore of 340,000 tonnes to 270,000 tonnes per month.
"Randfontein has been through the pain. That's finished with and Western Areas is still going through it now," Brownrigg said.
Randfontein's managing director Gordon Miller said underground recovery grades for the September quarter to date were up 14 percent and total costs were down 28 percent.

At Western Areas, recovered grades were seen improving due to mining of higher grade areas. Tonnes milled were expected to rise gradually to a monthly average of 250,000 tonnes while costs should decrease over the quarter.
H.J. Joel -- the low-cost jewel in JCI's golden crown and the only division to report a pre-capex net profit for the June quarter -- was consolidating its position, Brownrigg said.
"It's going to increase its throughput. It also has to control its costs which it's doing," he said.
